searchText: Does anyone happen to have the structure of a Transaction Receipt handy? The wiki appears to be missing a big section: https://eth.wiki/fundamentals/specs/consensus-datastructures 😆 Apparently I am the one that added that... https://github.com/ethereum/wiki/wiki/Consensus-Datastructures/6661590d7a850f28a5a723e6b9f1e94a7d2c89cc Why are transaction receipts sent over devp2p? Can't they be derived by every client? they can be derived, if you execute blocks from genesis. But if you do fast sync and get the snapshot, you cannot derive them and have to download, if you need them Which do people prefer? ``` rlp([a,b,c][]) ``` ``` rlp([a_0, b_0, c_0, ..., a_n, b_n, c_n]) ``` I feel like the former is easier to work with, and easier to describe in specifications (easier for humans), while the latter is a bit more compact on the wire since you don't have an extra byte for each of the inner arrays. If it matters, the number of items in the array is expected to be small (1 is the very common case, with a long tail out to perhaps ~256). I tend to prefer "easier for humans" over shaving 1-5% off of wire payloads, but I'm curious how others feel about that trade off.
